site.name: Great Northern Silver Mine
overview: Great Northern Silver Mine is the historic Great Northern Mine on the east side of Caribou Park, north of the former town of Caribou.
Federal geological studies document its shaft workings in the Caribou silver district and later retained the property among Boulder County's uranium-bearing vein localities.

timeline.text: The Great Northern was developed as part of the Caribou district's gold-and-silver mining landscape; federal reports describe the property as an established shaft mine north of Caribou.
U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 94 described the abandoned Great Northern shaft on the east side of Caribou Park, about a mile north of Caribou.

Federal uranium investigations revisited the Caribou area, mapped the Great Northern about 3,000 feet northeast of the Caribou mine, and retained Great Northern Silver Mine among Boulder County uranium-bearing vein occurrences.

moreHistory: USGS studies place the Great Northern on the contact of the Caribou stock and describe a substantial mine dump dominated by monzonite, evidence of significant underground development even though the workings were inaccessible during later federal visits.
The Great Northern name in the earlier Caribou mining literature and Great Northern Silver Mine in the later uranium compilation refer to the same Caribou-area mine locality retained by the registry.

A USGS/GNIS-derived mapped mine point at approximately 39.988598, -105.577778 is used as the historic mine-level identification anchor. It is a named mine locality, not a claim that a surviving shaft collar has been field surveyed or is safe to approach.
